seed.name: Glass Note
seed.text:
A good tasting note does not need to cosplay certainty: name the aroma, the texture, the finish, and what you would pour next. What did your glass actually say tonight?

FACT: TTB provides a public registry for looking up COLA records. https://www.ttb.gov/online-services/public-cola-registry

seed.name: Bar Craft
seed.text:
Bar craft lives in the small choices: glass, dilution, temperature, pace, and whether the bartender listens. Share the pour you would order twice, and tell us why.

FACT: TTB publishes an official Consumer Corner with alcohol-consumer education. https://www.ttb.gov/business-central/consumer

seed.name: Pace Check
seed.text:
Sober-curious is a real seat at the table, not a side quest: ask for a zero-proof build, take a night off, or just compare notes. What makes a no-alcohol option feel considered rather than apologetic?

FACT: TTB maintains a public consumer-education resource for alcohol topics. https://www.ttb.gov/business-central/consumer

seed.name: Batch Host
seed.text:
Batching is hospitality math with a human ending: keep the build clear, let people choose their pace, and make the nonalcoholic version just as intentional. What is your reliable party recipe—and what is the zero-proof sibling?

FACT: The official TTB registry is available online for public COLA-record lookup. https://www.ttb.gov/online-services/public-cola-registry

seed.name: Morning Kind
seed.text:
Hangover honesty is experience, not medicine: sometimes the lesson is “that was too fast,” “water would have helped,” or “today is an alcohol-free day.” No cures here—what boundary has made your next morning kinder?

FACT: TTB’s Consumer Corner is an official educational destination for consumers. https://www.ttb.gov/business-central/consumer

seed.name: Cork Watch
seed.text:
Wine talk gets better when “dry” is followed by something concrete: fruit, tannin, acid, body, or simply “not for me.” Which bottle taught you a useful new word?

FACT: TTB’s Public COLA Registry is an official public-facing lookup resource. https://www.ttb.gov/online-services/public-cola-registry

seed.name: Juniper Kid
seed.text:
Gin is a botanical argument: juniper leads, citrus interrupts, spice hangs around. What is your favorite gin-and-tonic adjustment, and what does it change in the glass?

FACT: TTB offers official consumer information through its Consumer Corner. https://www.ttb.gov/business-central/consumer

seed.name: Neat Pour
seed.text:
Whiskey notes are not a password test; “vanilla, oak, heat, and I like it” is a complete opening. Which detail makes you reach for another sip—and which makes you stop?

FACT: The TTB registry lets the public look up COLA records online. https://www.ttb.gov/online-services/public-cola-registry

seed.name: Cane Note
seed.text:
Rum can be bright, funky, grassy, molasses-rich, or all argument at once. What rum pour changed your assumptions, and would you serve it neat, tall, or in a stirred drink?

FACT: TTB’s official Consumer Corner is a place to start with consumer education. https://www.ttb.gov/business-central/consumer

seed.name: Zero Proof
seed.text:
A nonalc drink deserves its own flavor brief, not a consolation speech: bitter, tart, herbal, fizzy, or tea-deep all count. What is the best zero-proof serve you have had lately?

FACT: TTB provides an official online Consumer Corner for alcohol-related consumer education. https://www.ttb.gov/business-central/consumer
